newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS EXTENDS LEAD TO RECORD NINE IN MASTERS THIRD ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS EXTENDS LEAD TO RECORD NINE IN MASTERS THIRD ROUND.

text.p: Tiger Woods, displaying the cool bravado of a bullfighter and the delicate precision of a surgeon, methodically overpowered the Augusta National golf course on Saturday to lead the Masters by a record nine strokes after three rounds.

The 21-year-old Woods, playing in only his third Masters, shot a flawless seven-under-par 65 to tie the Masters 54-hole scoring record and leave the world's best golfers bobbing in his wake and struggling to find superlatives to describe their young rival.
It was the second consecutive day that Woods, making his Masters debut as a professional, posted the best round of the day following his 66 on Friday.
"He is like a boy amongst men and showing the men how to play," 47-year-old Tom Watson said after he shot a three-under-par 69 to move into a fourth-place tie -- 11 shots behind Woods.
The young sensation's closest pursuer was Costantino Rocca of Italy, who posted a rollercoaster 70 that gave him a 210 total and the honour of playing with Woods in the final round.
Paul Stankowski shot 69 to stand third, followed by veterans Tom Kite, who shot 66, and Tom Watson, who carded a 69.

Woods, seeking to become the youngest Masters champion, jumped out to a fast start and never looked back as the rest of the 46-man field failed to mount any kind of charge on a relatively benign golf course that was softened by overnight rain.

The three-time U.S. Amateur champion made four birdies on Augusta National's usually tough front nine and then added three more coming home, including one at the last, to take the biggest lead ever into the final round of the Masters.
The previous biggest 54-hole lead was fashioned by Raymond Floyd in 1976 on his way the tournament scoring record of 271.

"I'm really surprised that nobody made a run," Woods said after his amazing run of birdies, in which he used his awesome length off the tee to reduce Augusta's famed 6,925-yard course into something resembling a pitch-and-putt course.
"Right now I'm capitalising on my advantage," said Woods, whose drives average well over 300 yards.
"If I drive the ball well, I can be aggressive, spin the ball (on approaches) and hold my distances."
And that is exactly what he did.

He hit irons on his second shot on all four par-5s, making birdies on three, and wedges to the greens on most of the par-4s. He failed to birdie the 485-yard par-5 13th when he drove into trees on the right and went over the green with his second.

Rocca, a European Ryder Cup player who lost a playoff to John Daly in the 1995 British Open, gained second place by shooting five-under-par 31 on the back nine, where he made up five strokes in four holes, including two birdies and an eagle on the 11th through 12th holes -- Augusta's famed Amen Corner.
Stankowski also eagled the 13th hole and made a spectacular par save on the 500-yard 15th, where he hit his second shot over the green and into a pond beyond it.
"That was the shot of my career," he said of his pitch to within tap-in distance for par.
Woods meanwhile was oblivious to the record he established and the sensation he caused among the huge galleries, who gave him standing ovations at times.
"The only thing I want is a green jacket in my closet," he said before hurrying off -- to the practice range.
